newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: More S.Korean politicians go on trial for bribery.
newsitem.headline: More S.Korean politicians go on trial for bribery.

text.p: Another close political associate of South Korean President Kim Young-sam and seven serving or former lawmakers went on trial on Monday on charges of taking bribes from the founder of the controversial Hanbo group.
Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo, who was jailed last month for 15 years for a loans-for-kickbacks scandal, was again charged with bribing the politicians.
The scandal has already landed three close associates of the president -- one a former cabinet minister -- in jail along with bankers and businessmen.
Among eight politicians on trial on Monday was Moon Jung-soo, mayor of South Korea's second largest city, Pusan, a former secretary-general of Kim's ruling New Korea Party and two serving lawmakers.
Moon is a member of Kim's inner circle that played a leading role in his 1992 election victory.

State prosecutors accused the eight of accepting money from the founder of Hanbo, whose steel-making flagship collapsed in January under five trillion won ($5.6 billion) of debts, revealing a web of corruption.
They charged that Moon had received kickbacks of 200 million won before being elected as Pusan mayor in 1995.
A public furore over the Hanbo scandal led to the probe into President Kim's second son, Kim Hyun-chul, dealing a dire blow to Kim's presidency.
The prosecution has cleared Kim Hyun-chul of any involvement in the loans-for-kickbacks scandal, but arrested him on charges of bribery in unrelated cases and on tax evasion.
Opposition parties have alleged that Hanbo's Chung helped bankroll the president's 1992 election victory and that Kim Hyun-chul laundered huge sums of leftover funds through business cronies.
Kim Young-sam last month apologised for spending a large sum for his election campaign but refused to yield to opposition demands that he reveal details of his 1992 financing.
